A 22-year-old woman with no significant medical history presents with upper back pain lasting two
weeks. The pain worsens by the end of her workday, which involves prolonged periods of looking down
at her laptop. At its worst, the pain occasionally radiates into her neck. On examination, the left
transverse process just below the scapular spine becomes more posterior when the patient retracts her
shoulders and tilts her head upward. What is the most appropriate patient positioning and corrective
force for treatment? Answer Choices: (A) Patient seated with arms crossed, physician's hypothenar
eminences on bilateral T4 TPs, spine neutral, corrective force is posterior to anterior with left rotation
(B) Patient prone, physician's right thenar eminence on right T4 TP, left thumb on left T5 TP, extension
of spine, corrective force is diagonal from superior to inferior (C) Patient supine, physician's bilateral
thumbs on T4 TPs, patient's neck flexed, corrective force is oblique through patient's crossed arms (D)
Patient supine, physician's right thenar eminence under the left T4 TP, flex patient's spine and
sidebend to the left, corrective force is directed anterior to posterior through patient's crossed upper
extremities toward the left TP of T4 (E) Patient seated, physician's thumbs on bilateral T4 TPs, patient's
arms crossed, corrective force is anterior to posterior with rotation to the right (F) Patient prone with
arms at sides, physician's thenar eminences on bilateral T4 TPs, slight flexion, corrective force is
posterior to anterior with left translation (G) Patient prone, physician's left thenar eminence on patient's
left T4 TP, physician's right hypothenar eminence on right T5 TP, slight translation to the left, corrective
force is posterior to anterior straight down (H) Patient prone, head and neck rotated to the left,
physician's left thenar eminence on the left T4 TP, right hand on the left parietooccipital area, corrective
force into rotation from hand on head (I) Patient side-lying on right, physician's left thumb on left T4 TP,
flex patient's spine and rotate to the left, corrective force is lateral to medial through crossed arms (J)
Patient prone in extension, physician's thumbs on bilateral T4 TPs, slight right sidebending, corrective
force is straight anterior with right rotation
 A. Patient seated, physician's thumbs on bilateral T4 TPs, patient's arms crossed, corrective force is
anterior to posterior with rotation to the right
B. Patient prone, physician's left thenar eminence on patient's left T4 TP, physician's right
hypothenar eminence on right T5 TP, slight translation to the left, corrective force is posterior to
anterior straight down
C. Patient seated with arms crossed, physician's hypothenar eminences on bilateral T4 TPs, spine
neutral, corrective force is posterior to anterior with left rotation
D. Patient side-lying on right, physician's left thumb on left T4 TP, flex patient's spine and rotate to
the left, corrective force is lateral to medial through crossed arms
E. Patient prone with arms at sides, physician's thenar eminences on bilateral T4 TPs, slight flexion,
corrective force is posterior to anterior with left translation
F. Patient supine, physician's bilateral thumbs on T4 TPs, patient's neck flexed, corrective force is
oblique through patient's crossed arms
G. Patient supine, physician's right thenar eminence under the left T4 TP, flex patient's spine and
sidebend to the left, corrective force is directed anterior to posterior through patient's crossed upper
extremities toward the left TP of T4
H. Patient prone, head and neck rotated to the left, physician's left thenar eminence on the left T4
TP, right hand on the left parietooccipital area, corrective force into rotation from hand on head
I. Patient prone in extension, physician's thumbs on bilateral T4 TPs, slight right sidebending,
corrective force is straight anterior with right rotation

J. Patient prone, physician's right thenar eminence on right T4 TP, left thumb on left T5 TP,
extension of spine, corrective force is diagonal from superior to inferior
